subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: core event contracts and schema

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a dedicated core AI-safety taxonomy, minimally extend the existing generic diagnostic-event contract, or leave detector/evaluation taxonomies to plugins?
rationale: The choice establishes a long-lived core and plugin API contract and determines privacy, versioning, exporter, and compatibility responsibilities; source inspection cannot infer the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Extend existing diagnostics
options.body: Add only the generic typed fields and privacy rules required by current safety signals, reusing the established diagnostic-event and exporter pipeline.

options.title: Adopt dedicated taxonomy
options.body: Approve the proposed core event family and versioned schema as a first-class permanent OpenClaw contract, with explicit migration and plugin compatibility policy.

options.title: Keep taxonomy plugin-owned
options.body: Retain generic core diagnostics and let safety or evaluation plugins define specialized schemas through existing or narrowly extended SDK seams.

recommendation.title: Extend existing diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add only the generic typed fields and privacy rules required by current safety signals, reusing the established diagnostic-event and exporter pipeline.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to the original shared diagnostics architecture and its recent contract adjustment.
